speaker: EPILOGUE
text: I would now ask you how you like the play,

speaker: EPILOGUE
text: But, as it is with schoolboys, cannot say.

speaker: EPILOGUE
text: I am cruel fearful! Pray yet, stay a while,

speaker: EPILOGUE
text: And let me look upon you. No man smile?

speaker: EPILOGUE
text: Then it goes hard, I see. He that has

speaker: EPILOGUE
text: Loved a young handsome wench, then, show his

speaker: EPILOGUE
text: face—

speaker: EPILOGUE
text: ’Tis strange if none be here—and, if he will,

speaker: EPILOGUE
text: Against his conscience let him hiss and kill

speaker: EPILOGUE
text: Our market. ’Tis in vain, I see, to stay you.

speaker: EPILOGUE
text: Have at the worst can come, then! Now what say

speaker: EPILOGUE
text: you?

speaker: EPILOGUE
text: And yet mistake me not: I am not bold.

speaker: EPILOGUE
text: We have no such cause. If the tale we have told—

speaker: EPILOGUE
text: For ’tis no other—any way content you—

speaker: EPILOGUE
text: For to that honest purpose it was meant you—

speaker: EPILOGUE
text: We have our end; and you shall have ere long,

speaker: EPILOGUE
text: I dare say, many a better, to prolong

speaker: EPILOGUE
text: Your old loves to us. We, and all our might,

speaker: EPILOGUE
text: Rest at your service. Gentlemen, good night.
